classification.difficultyReason: Uses similar cones, subtraction of curved areas, algebraic factorisation and Pythagoras to derive frustum formulas.

content.prompt: The frustum of a cone has base radii $r$ and $R$, and the slant height is $s$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, upper-right cone and frustum figure

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let the slant height of the full cone be $\ell$. Show that $\ell=\dfrac{sR}{R-r}$.

answer.short:
$\ell=\dfrac{sR}{R-r}$.

Use corresponding radius and slant-height ratios in the similar cones.
answer.worked:
The removed cone has radius $r$ and slant height $\ell-s$. The cones are similar, so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\ell-s}{\ell}&=\frac{r}{R}\\R(\ell-s)&=r\ell\\R\ell-Rs&=r\ell\\\ell(R-r)&=Rs\\\ell&=\frac{sR}{R-r}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, show that the surface area of the curved section is $\pi(r+R)s$, and that the total surface area is $\pi(r^2+R^2)+\pi(r+R)s$.

answer.short:
Curved surface area: $\pi(r+R)s$.

Total surface area: $\pi(r^2+R^2)+\pi(r+R)s$.

Subtract the smaller cone’s curved area from the full cone’s, then add both circular ends.
answer.worked:
Subtract the curved area of the removed cone:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{curved}}&=\pi R\ell-\pi r(\ell-s)\\A_{\text{curved}}&=\pi\bigl((R-r)\ell+rs\bigr)\\A_{\text{curved}}&=\pi\left((R-r)\frac{sR}{R-r}+rs\right)\\A_{\text{curved}}&=\pi(Rs+rs)\\A_{\text{curved}}&=\pi(r+R)s.\end{align*}$$
Add the two circular ends:
$$\begin{align*}S&=\pi r^2+\pi R^2+A_{\text{curved}}\\S&=\pi(r^2+R^2)+\pi(r+R)s.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that the latter can be written as $\pi(r+R)\sqrt{(R-r)^2+h^2}+\pi(r^2+R^2)$, where $h$ is the height of the frustum.

answer.worked:
An axial section gives a right-angled triangle with legs $h$ and $R-r$ and hypotenuse $s$. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}s^2&=h^2+(R-r)^2\\s&=\sqrt{(R-r)^2+h^2}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the total surface area from part b:
$$\begin{align*}S&=\pi(r^2+R^2)+\pi(r+R)s\\S&=\pi(r+R)\sqrt{(R-r)^2+h^2}+\pi(r^2+R^2).\end{align*}$$
